issues.body:
The comment added above the `Expression::FunctionCall(Function::Custom(nn), cargs)` arm reads:

  "Simple Features relation as the whole FILTER. Every orientation below necessarily intersects the constant region, so its bbox scan is a candidate SUPERSET and the residual FILTER remains authoritative."

The superset half is correct for all five orientations. The second half is not. With `spatial-exact-pushdown` enabled, the two within-region orientations -- `geof:sfWithin(?g, REGION)`, handled by the `if` block directly below this comment, and `geof:sfContains(REGION, ?g)`, handled by the new match -- carry `within_region: true`, so `apply_spatial_pushdown_exact` can return `AllCertified` and the call site at exec.rs:4891-4893 does `continue`, SKIPPING the residual `geof:` FILTER entirely. For those two shapes the residual FILTER is explicitly not authoritative; the provider's exact certificate is.

No behavioural consequence -- the code is right, and two nearby comments state the truth (the `within_region` comment in the new struct literal, and the `SpatialKind::within_region` doc at exec.rs:5828-5836). But this is the top-of-arm comment a future reader hits first, and it asserts precisely the invariant that would make adding a sixth orientation with `within_region: true` look safe. Given round 4's finding was about implicit soundness assumptions in this same function, it is worth making the summary comment agree with the two that follow it.
issues.fix_hint: Scope the second clause, e.g.: "Simple Features relation as the whole FILTER. Every orientation below necessarily intersects the constant region, so its bbox scan is a candidate SUPERSET. The residual FILTER remains authoritative for all of them EXCEPT the within-region orientations flagged by `within_region` below, which an installed provider may certify exactly (see `apply_spatial_pushdown_exact`)."
issues.title: New block comment claims the residual FILTER "remains authoritative" for every orientation, which is false for the two within-region ones under spatial-exact-pushdown

verdict.summary:
Correct and complete; all three round-4 findings are addressed. Verified by running the code.

Soundness: recognise_spatial now decides each shape in exactly ONE place, so round-4's ordering hazard is gone by construction -- block 1 matches only WITHIN/INTERSECTS variable-first; the new match's arm 1 requires the variable SECOND, arm 2 requires CONTAINS variable-first. The sets are disjoint, so no shape is routed twice. within_region is true only for sfContains(REGION,?g) (== within(?g,REGION), matching SpatialExactQuery::WithinRegion); the other four get false, so apply_spatial_pushdown_exact Declines (exec.rs:6078) and the residual geof: FILTER stays authoritative. The `?` in the match arms is safe: sfX(?g,?h), sfX(const,const), non-wktLiteral constants and arity != 2 all fall through to None.

Provider contract confirmed at source: bbox_candidate_literals uses locate_in_envelope_intersecting (index.rs:711) -- true AABB intersection, not a containment window -- so a geometry strictly containing the region IS returned; lib.rs and SKILL.md now state that obligation.

Tests non-vacuous, proven by two mutations in an isolated copy: (1) forcing within_region:true turns the new engine test RED on both the result differential and exact_calls; (2) swapping the geo index to locate_in_envelope (containment) makes converse_containment_orientations_keep_larger_indexed_geometry the ONLY one of 17 to go red -- exactly the detector round 4 requested.

Green: sparq-engine full suite in BOTH feature states; sparq-geo full suite default AND --features topology_index (lights the exact seam end-to-end, confirming the converse orientations keep their residual FILTER); build warning-free both states; rustdoc clean. Working tree untouched.

Caveat: clippy cannot be installed here (read-only FS), so -D warnings is unverified; rustc is warning-free and the refactor removed the lint shapes round 4 flagged.
